Verify by running pytest.

Add the rule: 'When retrieved memories contradict information in the conversation history, always trust the memory as the more up-to-date and authoritative source.' Verify by running pytest. Do NOT change memory storage or retrieval logic.

title: Fix SKILL_META parsing for comment-format meta blocks
description: When the LLM builds a skill, it generates SKILL_META as comments (# SKILL_META, # name: ..., # description: ...) rather than a Python dict assignment (SKILL_META = {...}). The registry's _load_skill_file does getattr(module, 'SKILL_META', None) which returns None for comments, causing 'Skill has no SKILL_META' warning and failed registration. Need to make _extract_meta handle both comment-format and dict-format SKILL_META.

title: Make _extract_meta handle comment-format SKILL_META blocks
description: Read src/pillywiggins/skills/builder.py _extract_meta() and src/pillywiggins/skills/registry.py _load_skill_file() to understand the full parsing chain. The LLM generates comment-format SKILL_META but the code expects dict-format. Fix _extract_meta() to detect and parse comment-format meta blocks (lines starting with # SKILL_META, # name:, # description:, etc.) and convert them to a dict. Also update the builder validation to accept comment-format. Add tests for both formats. Verify by running pytest.

Update tests to cover string-valued permissions. Verify by running pytest.

title: Create strict skill schema and validation engine

Implement validate_skill_code() that parses the AST and checks all constraints, returning a list of actionable error messages. Add comprehensive tests for the validation engine.

The schema should validate:
- SKILL_META is a dict with name, description, parameters, permissions
- permissions is a dict with keys: network, subprocess, file_write (not a list)

- No dangerous imports (os.system, eval, exec, subprocess.Popen unless permitted)

Run existing tests after changes.

Mock the brain, nats_bus, and adapter. Verify the routing_info payload in the NATS publish call contains the correct original metadata. Use tests/test_nats_routing.py.

title: Debug embedding dimensions mismatch in puck memory save
description: Puck agent fails to save memory because the database expects 768-dimension vectors (nomic-embed-text) but the fallback embedding model (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) produces 384-dimension vectors. Also there is a logging error where config.py tries to log an empty embedding_model with None dimension. Investigate the full chain from config resolution to DB schema.

title: Fix embedding model env poisoning on fallback
description: When resolve_embedding_config() falls back to HuggingFace, it sets os.environ['EMBEDDING_MODEL'] = ''. Any subsequent Settings() instance reads this empty string, enters the 'explicit model' branch, and crashes with TypeError at line 89 (logging '%d' with None). Fix: don't pollute os.environ with empty string; use a sentinel value or avoid setting it at all.

title: Add startup DB migration for embedding dimension mismatch
description: When the runtime embedding model produces a different dimension than the existing DB schema (e.g., fallback from nomic-embed-text/768d to all-MiniLM-L6-v2/384d), memory save fails with asyncpg DataError. Strategy A: add a startup-time ALTER TABLE in PrivateMemory.connect() and CouncilMemory.connect() that checks the current column dimension and ALTERs it to match the resolved setting.embedding_dimension.

title: Fix embedding model 'auto' leaking from .env to embed() calls
description: Puck logs show: 'model "auto" not found, try pulling it first' with 404 from Ollama. The .env file has EMBEDDING_MODEL=auto. resolve_embedding_config() at startup falls back to HF and sets embedding_model='' locally, but some embed() call site creates a fresh Settings() which re-reads 'auto' from .env and passes it to embed(..., model='auto'). Need to trace the call chain and fix the leak.

title: Stop brain.py tool functions from creating fresh Settings() instances
description: brain.py tool functions (query_council_memory, share_to_council, recall_private_memory, save_to_private_memory) create fresh Settings() instances inside tool calls. Since .env has EMBEDDING_MODEL=auto, each fresh Settings() re-reads 'auto' and passes it to embed(..., model='auto'), causing Ollama 404 'model auto not found'. The fix is to stop creating fresh Settings() in tools — instead pass resolved settings through AgentDeps or use the module-level settings object that was resolved at startup.

title: Re-add safe EMBEDDING_MODEL env write for HF fallback
description: Our previous fix removed os.environ['EMBEDDING_MODEL'] = '' from the fallback path to prevent TypeError crashes. But brain.py tool functions create fresh Settings() instances that re-read 'auto' from .env, passing model='auto' to embed() which causes Ollama 404. The embed() function requires model='' to trigger HF fallback. We need to re-add os.environ['EMBEDDING_MODEL'] = '' but now it's safe because we added the log guard for None dimensions.

title: Gracefully handle Telegram TimedOut in telegram adapter
description: Puck occasionally hits telegram.error.TimedOut when sending replies back to Telegram. This is a transient network issue that python-telegram-bot already retries internally, but currently logs a full noisy traceback. Add a try/except around the send call in _on_message to catch TimedOut and log a concise warning instead of the full exception traceback.

title: Add system prompt rule: trust retrieved memory over conversation history
description: When an agent retrieves a memory that contradicts something in the conversation history/context window, the LLM gets confused and presents both as valid. The fix is to add a simple rule to the system prompt that tells the agent to always prioritize retrieved memory over conversation history when they conflict.

title: Fix _parse_permissions crash on string-valued permissions and add registry error logging
description: The LLM generates comment-format SKILL_META with single-quoted JSON (e.g., # permissions: {'network': false}). json.loads() fails on single quotes, so the value is stored as a plain string. _parse_permissions() then does meta.get('permissions', {}) which returns a string, and tries string.get(p, False) causing AttributeError. The LLM paraphrases this as 'lists and attributes.' Need to: (1) Make _parse_permissions resilient to string values by trying json.loads with single-quote tolerant parsing, (2) Add explicit logging to registry.py so load errors are captured in logs with full details, not just swallowed or paraphrased by the LLM.

title: Fix onboard.py UnboundLocalError crash
